includes: Every screen on this page, on one account
Offline till that keeps selling when the signal drops

hero.eyebrow: Built for Kenyan wholesalers & large retailers
hero.title: Sell, split the payment, keep the stock honest.
hero.lede: A phone-first shop system for the person at the till, not just the owner with a laptop. Take a sale across cash, M-Pesa and card, let a known customer go into credit, keep expiry and stock straight, and print a KRA eTIMS receipt that adds up to the shilling.
notes: No build step inside the prototype — one self-contained file, works offline
Sample data, in memory: reload resets it

stats.label: payment parts
stats.note: cash, M-Pesa, card on one sale

features.title: Split payments, honestly
features.body: Up to three payment parts per sale, each with its own amount and a Fill/Rest button that inserts what is still unpaid. Overpay and the till shows change; come up short and it asks who is taking the credit — a walk-in cannot hold one.

features.title: A till that fits a thumb
features.body: Designed at 360 px first, then allowed to grow. 52 px steppers, inputmode="numeric" quantity fields that select on focus, and a bottom tab bar instead of a cramped sidebar.

features.title: Stock that actually counts
features.body: Quantity is a count, not a delta — the sheet says so. Quick-add chips for +1/+6/+12/+24/+48, reorder levels, expiry dates, and low/out-of-stock surfaced on the dashboard before a customer asks.

features.title: The customer is on the receipt
features.body: Pick a customer at the till, add one on the spot, or type a name for a walk-in. Whatever is chosen is what prints under Customer on the receipt, and a walk-in keeps no balance so it can never take credit.

features.title: Migration without tears
features.body: Three real .xlsx templates with coloured header rows. Preview and a row-by-row validation report before a single write; three bad dates are reported as three rows, not a failed import. One press undoes the batch.

features.title: eTIMS that never blocks the till
features.body: Sign locally, transmit asynchronously, retry with backoff. Device and PIN block on its own screen, test transmission, and every signature on the receipt.

money.title: The rules that keep the money honest
money.body: Every figure on screen is a real sum of stored rows. Round each line to two decimals, then sum — never the other way round.

cases.title: Paid in full
cases.detail: One method, blank amount means the exact total. The cashier never types the same number twice.

cases.title: Overpaid
cases.detail: Cash Ksh 1,000 against a Ksh 980 basket. Change is shown; credit is untouched.

cases.title: Come up short
cases.detail: The till asks who is taking the credit, then writes the difference to that customer's balance and decrements stock.

cases.title: Credit turned off
cases.detail: If the shop has 'allow credit' off, a shortfall cannot complete at all — and a walk-in can never hold a balance.

templates.columns: sku, name, category, unit, cost_price, selling_price, opening_qty, reorder_level, expiry_date, supplier, barcode
name, phone, credit_limit, opening_balance, since, notes
receipt_no, date, customer, sku, qty, unit_price, amount_paid, payment_method, cashier, notes

rules: Dates: accept YYYY-MM-DD, dd/mm/yyyy (the Kenyan convention — never read as mm/dd) and bare Excel serial integers.
Reject anything else by row number with the value shown. Never guess, never silently swap day and month.
A sale dated in the future is rejected; an expiry date in the future is of course fine.
An imported sale keeps its own date — it lands in that quarter's report and never in today's takings.
A duplicate receipt_no or sku is skipped, never doubled, and reported.
Failed rows are left out, the rest go in, and the report says how many of each.

data_model.note: Postgres. Money as numeric(12,2). Timestamps as timestamptz, business dates as plain date — a receipt belongs to a day, not an instant.
data_model.sql:
shop            (id, name, branch, phone, kra_pin, plan_kes, plan_renews_on, created_at)
user            (id, shop_id, name, phone unique, role enum('owner','sales'),
                 password_hash, active, last_seen_at)
category        (id, shop_id, name, position)
product         (id, shop_id, sku, name, category_id, unit, cost_price, selling_price,
                 qty, reorder_level, expiry_date, barcode, created_at, updated_at)
supplier        (id, shop_id, name, phone, terms, balance_owed)
purchase_order  (id, shop_id, supplier_id, no, status, ordered_on, received_on, total)
customer        (id, shop_id, name, phone, credit_limit, balance, since, notes)
sale            (id, shop_id, receipt_no, sold_at, sold_on, customer_id, cashier_id,
                 subtotal, vat, total, credit_amount, created_at)
sale_line       (id, sale_id, product_id, name_snapshot, qty, unit_price,
                 unit_cost_snapshot)
sale_payment    (id, sale_id, method, amount)
payment         (id, shop_id, customer_id, received_at, amount, method, user_id)
expense         (id, shop_id, spent_on, description, category, amount)
etims_transmission (id, sale_id, status, signature, sent_at, response)
audit_entry     (id, shop_id, user_id, at, action, detail)
rules: sale_line snapshots name, price and cost. Editing a product later must not rewrite history.
receipt_no is unique per shop and never reused, even after a void.
customer.balance is derived but stored — recalculated nightly and in every test.
sale.credit_amount is an explicit column so the credit figure cannot drift.

deploy.summary: This page is built and published by GitHub Actions. One setting has to be switched on by hand, once; after that every push to main rebuilds and redeploys.

manual_steps.action: Under Build and deployment, set Source to GitHub Actions.
manual_steps.note: This is the only manual step. Without it the workflow runs, uploads an artifact and fails at deploy.

automatic: ubuntu-latest + Node 24 installs nothing (zero dependencies) and runs node build.js.
The build renders index.html, resolves the internal-link check and copies the prototype and the spec into dist/.
actions/upload-pages-artifact packages dist/, actions/deploy-pages publishes it, and the run URL is printed in the step summary.

footer.note: Sample data in the prototype is a Mombasa wholesale shop, not lorem ipsum. Every figure derives from it, so changing the seed changes every number on screen.
